description.p: LinNote is a scratchpad for Linux built for typing rather than clicking. Notes live in pages you switch with the keyboard, and each page can be a plain note, a checklist, a code block with highlighting, a markdown document, a timer or a calculator.
Finish a line with an equals sign and the calculator answers in place. It reads a comma or a dot as the decimal point, following your locale, and the same line converts units and currencies.
A page can be locked with a password. Locked pages are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and the key is derived from the password with PBKDF2.

description.p: The uninstaller asks before it removes anything and keeps your notes unless you ask for them to go. It used to delete them with no confirmation.
Locked notes are now encrypted with AES-256-GCM instead of the reversible scheme used in 1.0.0, and existing locked notes are converted the first time they are opened.
The calculator reads a comma as the decimal point, so 1,5 + 2,3 answers 3,8 instead of 1.
The global shortcut now binds on GNOME, and the app no longer writes note or clipboard contents to the system log.
